_readme: Named look presets. Pick one with RUFUS_STYLE=<name>; the text is used as
the stills detail suffix, exactly as if it had been pasted into
RUFUS_STILLS_DETAIL. A literal RUFUS_STILLS_DETAIL still wins over a
preset name, so a one-off experiment never has to be added here first.
These are LOOKS, not subjects. The niche decides what the video is about;
a style decides how it is drawn. money_history rendered as stickman is a
different channel from money_history rendered flat-vector, and neither
needs a change to the research, the script or the storyboard.
A style has to be describable in ONE block of text that is appended to
every prompt byte for byte. That is not a limitation of this file — it is
how look consistency works at all: an image model renders each beat from
noise with no memory of the others, so two paraphrases of one style are
stickman: Minimalist stick-figure cartoon illustration drawn in thin, clean black line art of uniform weight. COLOUR IS FLAT, SATURATED AND REAL: grass is green, sky is a clear light blue with a few simple white clouds, earth and sand are warm brown, water is blue, stone is grey. Fill every shape with solid colour edge to edge. Never wash the background out, never draw it paler or thinner than the foreground, and never leave it as bare paper — a scene where only the figure is finished looks unfinished. The background is quieter than the subject because it is simpler and further away, not because it is faded. SCALE: the figures carrying this moment stand between half and three quarters of the frame's height, near the camera, so a face and a pose read at a glance on a phone held at arm's length. The place is built BEHIND them, never instead of them — a wide landscape with a small figure off to one side is a picture of a landscape, and the beat it was drawn for is about the person. Every figure has a perfect oval head slightly taller than wide with a white fill and a thin black outline, two solid black oval dot eyes evenly spaced in the upper-middle third of the face, two short straight eyebrow strokes above them, and one thin curved line for the mouth — and nothing else: no nose, no ears, no cheek lines, no hair, completely bald and smooth. THE FACE CARRIES THE EMOTION OF THE MOMENT and must not be the same on every figure: brows angled down and inward over a flat or down-curved mouth for anger, brows raised high over a small open oval mouth for shock, brows slanted up at their inner ends over a downward mouth curve for worry or grief, a wide upturned curve with the eyes squeezed to short arcs for delight, brows flat and mouth a short straight line for cold indifference. The pose carries it too: shoulders thrown up, arms reaching, back hunched, head dropped, one figure leaning away from another. The body is a stick figure built from FLAT FILLED SHAPES, not from bare lines: a narrow white torso with the same clean black outline as the head, thin white arms that bend once at the elbow, thin white legs that bend once at the knee, small simple hands, a short neck. Every part is white fill inside an outline, exactly the way the head is — never a naked pen stroke with nothing inside it, and never two different constructions in one picture. No muscle lines, no shading, no rounded 3D volume. PROPORTION IS FIXED AND DOES NOT DRIFT BETWEEN SHOTS: the head is about one third of the whole figure's height, the torso line about one third, and the legs the remaining third. The arms leave the torso just under the neck and reach to mid-thigh. A head that is half the body in one shot and a tenth of it in the next reads as two different characters rather than one. Clothing is drawn as simple line-art garments with flat unshaded colour fills inside the outlines only. ANIMALS AND OBJECTS ARE DRAWN PROPERLY, and this contrast is the whole charm of the style: the PEOPLE stay simple stick figures, while anything that is NOT a person — an animal, a machine, a vehicle, a building, an object — is a real illustration with its true shape, proportions and markings, whatever that thing happens to be in this particular shot. Same clean black outline, same flat saturated fills, but drawn with care and detail a stick figure never gets. BEHIND THE FIGURES, BUILD THE WHOLE PLACE. Every frame is a complete scene, not a figure floating on paper: a ground plane filling the bottom third to half of the frame, a horizon line across it, and open sky above. On the ground and along the horizon go the four to eight things that say where THIS shot's place is, taken from the shot's own description and from nothing else. Draw them in the same clean black line art as everything else. THE PLACE PERSISTS: consecutive shots in one location keep the same horizon height, the same colours and the same landmarks, so the sequence reads as one world seen from different angles rather than a new drawing each time. No gradients, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no texture, no photographic lighting, no depth of field, no film grain. Bold, readable silhouettes; the whole frame reads instantly at thumbnail size. NO LETTERING ANYWHERE IN THE FRAME: nothing written, printed, stamped, carved or painted, in any alphabet, on anything. Whatever THIS shot happens to contain that would normally carry writing is drawn BLANK, with at most a few wordless ruled lines. Garbled words are the single clearest sign a machine made the picture.
flat_vector: Flat 2D vector illustration style, not a photograph: clean confident outlines of consistent stroke weight, simplified geometric shapes rendered in flat, unshaded color fills. No gradients, no photographic lighting, no film grain, no lens blur or depth of field, no skin pores or fabric-weave texture. Figures and objects are graphic and stylized rather than anatomically photographic — bold silhouettes, minimal internal linework, an expressive pose read through shape and posture. Lighting is rendered as bold graphic contrast — a hard-edged light shape or color-block shadow — never a soft photographic gradient. Backgrounds simplify into clean shapes and generous negative space rather than photographic clutter. Reads like modern explainer-video or storybook illustration: crisp, deliberate, and stylized, never a photograph or a photo-real render. BUILD THE WHOLE SCENE, never a subject floating on blank paper: a ground plane filling the lower third to half of the frame, a horizon across it, sky above, and the four to eight things that say where this is. Colour is FLAT and SATURATED and fills every shape edge to edge — no gradients, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no texture, no photographic lighting, no depth of field, no film grain. The background is quieter than the subject because it is simpler and further away, never because it is faded or paler. Consecutive shots in one place keep the same horizon height, colours and landmarks. Bold, readable silhouettes; the whole frame reads instantly at thumbnail size. ink_woodcut: Monochrome ink woodcut engraving, the look of a 19th-century newspaper illustration. Dense parallel hatching and cross-hatching for every tone; no grey fills, no gradients, no colour. Heavy confident contour lines, fine interior hatching, deep blacks against untouched white paper. Slight plate texture and ink bleed at the line edges. Figures are solid and weighty, drawn with anatomical confidence rather than stylisation. Reads like a printed engraving lifted from an 1890s broadsheet. No gradients, no depth of field, no film grain, no lens blur, no ambient occlusion, no 3D render — this is a print, not a photograph of one. BUILD THE WHOLE SCENE, never a figure floating on blank paper: a ground under the figures, a horizon across it, and the four to eight things that say where THIS shot's place is, taken from the shot's own description and from nothing else. The background is drawn with FEWER strokes than the subject, never with fainter ones: it is quieter because it is simpler and further away, not because it is washed out. paper_cut: Paper-cutout collage illustration, as if every element were scissored from sheets of coloured construction paper and laid in layers. Each shape is a clean flat silhouette with a slightly rough torn or cut edge and a soft drop shadow one or two pixels down and right, so the layers read as real paper stacked on paper. People are simple rounded cutout figures with dot eyes and a single curved mouth line, their limbs separate paper pieces. Warm saturated palette: mustard yellow, tomato red, teal, cream and deep navy, with the sky a single flat sheet. Objects and animals are cut with care and keep their real proportions and markings. chalkboard: White and pastel chalk drawing on a deep slate-green board. Every line is a slightly grainy chalk stroke with soft edges and visible texture where the chalk caught the board, and the board itself shows faint smudges and eraser sweeps in the empty areas. People are simple chalk stick figures with dot eyes and drawn brows. Accents in dusty yellow, coral, sky blue and mint, used sparingly against the white. Diagrams, arrows and simple labelled shapes are welcome — this is the look of a good teacher mid-explanation. Objects and animals are drawn properly with real proportions. Bold confident outlines of varying weight, shapes filled with flat ink and the occasional coarse halftone dot field where a mid-tone is needed, plus a deliberate one-or-two-pixel misregistration on some fills as though a plate slipped. People are simple stylised figures with strong silhouettes and minimal faces. Mid-century geometric shapes: long shadows, simplified architecture, stylised clouds and hills. storybook: Children's picture-book illustration in soft gouache: hand-painted flat shapes with a visible brushed edge, gentle warm colours — butter yellow, sage, dusty rose, cornflower blue, soft brown — and a thin uneven ink line over the top on the important shapes only. People are simple round-headed figures with dot eyes, drawn brows and a single mouth line, warm and friendly. Animals and objects are painted with real care and keep their true shapes and markings. Everything is calm, generous and a little hand-made; nothing is mechanical or vector-perfect. ink_explainer: Hand-drawn marker-and-ink cartoon illustration — the look of a very good sketchbook page, loose and warm and confident, never vector-clean. THE LINE IS DRAWN BY HAND: a dark ink stroke of VARYING weight that wobbles slightly, thickens on the contours and at the corners, and sometimes overshoots where two lines meet. Nothing is ruler-straight or compass-round. PEOPLE ARE STICK FIGURES and stay that way: a white oval head slightly taller than wide with a thin ink outline, two solid black dot eyes, two short drawn eyebrow strokes, one curved line for the mouth, a loose scribble of hair on top, one straight line for the torso, thin arms and legs angled at the elbow and the knee, small simple hands. No nose, no ears, no cheek lines. THE FACE CARRIES THE EMOTION OF THE MOMENT and must not be the same on every figure: brows angled down and inward over a flat mouth for anger, brows raised high over a small open oval mouth for fear or shock, brows slanted up at their inner ends over a downward mouth curve for worry or grief, eyes squeezed to short arcs over a wide upturned curve for delight, brows flat and mouth a short straight line for cold indifference. Clothing is drawn ON the stick figure as one simple garment — a fur wrap, a coat, an apron — filled with scribbled texture rather than with flat colour. ANIMALS AND OBJECTS ARE DRAWN PROPERLY, and this contrast is the whole charm of the style: the PEOPLE stay stick figures while anything that is NOT a person — an animal, a vehicle, a building, an object — keeps its true shape, its real proportions and its own markings, whatever that thing happens to be in this particular shot: the same hand-drawn ink line, but drawn with a care a stick figure never gets. THE SCENE IS FULLY PAINTED AND CARRIES THE WEATHER: never a figure standing on blank paper but a place with its own light and its own mood — rain as long diagonal strokes across the whole frame, floodwater as brown current with white streak lines through it, a fire as warm orange light thrown on a dark cave wall, night as deep blue. Colour goes on like marker over the ink: mostly flat but with the stroke texture left visible, and SHADING IS SCRIBBLED — pencil-like hatching and dense scribble wherever this shot's own scene is dark, never a smooth blend. THE WHOLE FRAME CARRIES ONE TEMPERATURE: cold grey-blue for a storm, warm ochre for firelight, fresh green and white for a clear day. Big bold hand-drawn arrows, circles and simple marks are welcome where a shot needs to point at something, drawn in the same thick wobbling ink and never as clean vector shapes. No gradients, no depth of field, no film grain, no lens blur, no ambient occlusion, no 3D render, no photographic lighting. BUILD THE WHOLE SCENE, never a figure floating on blank paper: a ground under the figures, a horizon or a back wall behind them, and the four to eight things that say where THIS shot's place is, taken from the shot's own description and from nothing else.
